findings.summary: Candidate eedcbb2 (coding attempt 2) is not acceptable. 6 of the 14 new tests fail, there is no native evidence, and Root's three suspicions are all confirmed by reading the code. (1) family-space calls the bridge reader with the legacy two-argument signature, so every bridge introduction returns 503. (2) Activation refuses any unacknowledged review row, so a stale fenced intent permanently blocks a valid source. (3) The React held-response test goes through focus, and focus already invalidates opens. The two other failing groups are test-harness defects: a cooldown/clock problem in the UI tests, and parent-only queue actions sent through founderCommand. The diff also adds an unconditional setEntry(null) in read(), which closes any opened introduction or saved play on every poll and turns the existing retention logic into dead code. ACK and absence rows can be deleted without the schema noticing. Many mandatory negative and positive controls (journal, corruption, races, rollback stages, legacy control) are missing. The core structure is close to the setup contract: original-key lookup before acquisition, prelock order, real kernel consume, booking CAS, sealed fact with append after commit, absence retirement and branded adapter. The attempt-3 corrections below are bounded.

findings.title: Family adventure() calls bridge readRevision with the legacy 2-arg signature
findings.problem: adventure() picks `reader=state.ownership==='bridge'?bridgeRevision:revision` and calls `reader(tx,{household_id,...payload_ref})`. Bridge readRevision is `(tx,input,descriptor)`, so the descriptor arrives as parentScope input: ownData rejects the extra keys and descriptor is undefined. That throws, the throw is caught by adventure's catch-all, and the result is fail() → 503. This is exactly the observed 'Synthetic family space unavailable' at family-space.mjs:40 in 3 failing tests (positive path, frozen content, sibling control). No authenticated introduction can open, so the slice's core outcome and acceptance fail.
findings.fix_check: Call `bridgeRevision(tx,bridgeScope(s),descriptor)` with the exact 7-field descriptor, and keep `revision(tx,descriptor)` only for unbridged rows. The positive path test, frozen-content test and sibling control pass, with the legacy resolver call count at 0 (see the legacy-control finding).

findings.title: Activation rejects every historical unACKed review row, not live pending
findings.problem: assertBridgeActivation fails with conflict if `selected.rows.some(x=>!x.row.ack)` for the request. Review never ACKs fenced or superseded intents. finish() deliberately preserves them as forensic rows (lines 280-295, 336, 343), and livePending already filters them out. Any request that ever had a fenced review command (outage followed by an edit, a stale retry, a demoted actor) can therefore never be activated, even after a fresh valid all-true review and acknowledged release. The spec requires 'no pending source facts', meaning live pending under current authority, and forbids stale-intent retirement on acquisition. acquireBridgeSource inherits the same refusal.
findings.fix_check: Use the owning livePending/pending(tx,rows,a,s,currentPin) semantics instead of a blanket !ack check. Add a test: a real review intent fenced by an outage plus edit, then fresh review and release → acquisition and activation succeed. A genuinely live pending intent still conflicts, and table hashes are unchanged on refusal.

findings.title: read() now clears the open entry unconditionally on every refresh/poll
findings.problem: The added `++openSequence.current;setEntry(null);` runs on every read(): the 15 s interval, focus, pageshow, visibilitychange and capture acknowledgement. The existing line-99 logic deliberately kept an open introduction or saved-play receipt when it was still ready and confirmed. That logic is now dead, because entry is already null when it runs. Any opened introduction or saved play (accepted 07-A/07-B flows) is closed within 15 s or on focus. The spec only requires invalidating held older open RESPONSES (the sequence increment), not destroying a displayed, still-valid entry. This regresses accepted behaviour without any test.
findings.fix_check: Keep `++openSequence.current` at read start, but remove the unconditional setEntry(null) so the post-read retention filter decides. Add a DOM test: an open introduction survives a healthy refresh, and is cleared when the newer read reports pending or withdrawn.

findings.title: Held-response React test uses focus, so the new read() fence is untested
findings.problem: The test dispatches window focus. Focus calls refresh(), which already increments openSequence at LoopFamilyHome.tsx:105 (existing code), so the test would pass without the new read() invalidation. Spec requirement 'FamilyHome increments/invalidate its open sequence when a newer read begins' therefore has no meaningful regression coverage. The test also fails earlier, in the harness (separate finding).
findings.fix_check: Trigger a newer read that does not go through refresh, for example LoopRequestStatus onObserved/captureAcknowledged after a real request-status view, or child reselection. Assert that the held open resolves without rendering and the newer pending/withdrawn read is shown. Prove that the test fails if line 93's increment is removed.

findings.title: UI harness reuses a consumed join token because the clock never advances
findings.problem: The generation fixture's access policy has resendCooldownMs:1 and a frozen fake clock. The harness posts a 'recover' request at the same instant, so no new token is delivered, and mockInbox still holds the already-consumed join token. /adult/verify then returns 200 'invalid' with no Set-Cookie, which causes the observed `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'split')`. Both HTTP and React tests therefore never ran any bridge assertion. The existing family test advances `at+=2` before recovery.
findings.fix_check: Call f.advance(≥2) before /adult/request, assert that a new inbox token differs from the previous one, and assert that Set-Cookie exists with HttpOnly/SameSite/Path. Both UI tests reach their bridge assertions and pass.

findings.title: Queue post-ready test sends parent-only actions via founderCommand
findings.problem: In request-queue.mjs:24, CorrectRequest and CancelRequest are parent (familyCommand) shapes, and only RequestClarification, ProposeAlternative, AcceptRequest, DeclineRequest and PrepareLateUpdate are founder shapes. The test sends CorrectRequest through founderCommand and gets validation_failed, never the new post-ready guard: this is the observed failure. As written, the test also never checks that an ORIGINAL pre-ready command key still replays after readiness, despite its name. Its late-update check only compares bridge status, not receipt/due/ready_at/family clocks or the sent=false state.
findings.fix_check: Send CorrectRequest/CancelRequest/AgreeAlternative/AnswerClarification via familyCommand with real selection/session, and founder actions via founderCommand. Each fresh key returns conflict with unchanged table hashes. Replay the original AcceptRequest key and get its original acknowledged result. After PrepareLateUpdate, assert unchanged receipt, original_due_at, ready_at, ACK and delivery not_attempted, and that the late update has sent=false.

findings.title: ACK and absence rows can be deleted without schema or service detection
findings.problem: The immutability triggers are BEFORE UPDATE only. private_bridge_guard checks primary completeness, absences over 64 and absence/command coexistence, but not the existence of an ACK for an independently recorded fact, nor that absence markers are retained. A DELETE of private_bridge_acks silently turns an acknowledged readiness back into pending, and a later reconcile re-appends the same fact. A DELETE of private_bridge_absences re-enables a late insertion that was retired. history() also does not quarantine 'independent record present but ACK missing'. The spec requires missing acknowledged history to quarantine and retirement to persist, with bypass-negative tests.
findings.fix_check: Reject DELETE on the bridge tables except through household cascade (for example a BEFORE DELETE trigger that allows it only when the household row is gone), or make the service quarantine an independent record whose ACK is missing. Add bypass tests: deleting an ACK, an absence or a delivery-work row is refused or quarantined, with unchanged hashes and no re-append.

findings.title: Mandatory journal controls are mostly missing
findings.problem: The only journal test covers cross-domain empty adoption (review store opened as bridge, and the reverse). The spec requires: wrong household key and wrong operator key on the bridge store, populated wrong-domain adoption, corruption and truncation quarantine with unchanged bytes, one-use adoption, sticky whole-instance quarantine, healthy reopen controls, and key-copy wiping after construction, each operation, exceptions and close, without zeroing provider master buffers. None of these are exercised. The wipe() design (clearing all owned buffers after each serialized operation) is plausible but unverified.
findings.fix_check: Add tests for each listed control. Instrument provider buffers to prove they are unchanged after close, and capture derived buffers through a test hook to prove they are zeroed after success, failure and close. Refusals leave bytes unchanged and are paired with healthy controls.

findings.title: Required source, race, rollback and quarantine tests are absent
findings.problem: The following spec checks are missing: (a) acquisition racing a new running generation head conflicts, with no generation recovery and unchanged hashes; (b) strict activation rejects stale generation, profile, scope, agreement, checklist, pending release and a withdrawn selected snapshot (only output_digest and review_version are tested); (c) failure at each primary stage (core insert, capacity CAS, bridge rows, seal) rolls back with zero append (only a post-kernel throw is tested); (d) altered materialized rows, missing ACK history and namespace mismatch quarantine without republishing; (e) corrupt bridge or review history makes the whole child home return 503, separately from healthy pending/withdrawn item states; (f) namespace-only ownership (core private-bridge payload without binding) gives 503 with no fallback; (g) a profile correction closes availability.
findings.fix_check: Add focused tests for (a)–(g), each paired with a valid control and hash or count assertions.

findings.title: Missing-adapter test cannot detect legacy fallback; no unbridged control
findings.problem: familyWith's legacy content.revision throws, and family adventure() maps any throw to 503. A fallback to the legacy resolver is therefore indistinguishable from the correct 503. The spec requires 'zero legacy resolver calls' plus a paired unbridged legacy positive control that still succeeds. Neither a call counter nor a legacy positive control exists.
findings.fix_check: Count legacy resolver calls in the fixture and assert 0 for bridged, namespace-only, missing-adapter and pending cases. Add an unbridged seeded-legacy record that opens through the counting resolver (count 1) on the same bridge-enabled family.

findings.title: pending_readiness is not shown to the parent
findings.problem: The server adds allowance.pending_readiness, but the allowance card does not render it and the Allowance type omits it. The request card does say 'Readiness awaiting confirmation', but the consumed allowance is shown without explaining that part of it is awaiting confirmation.
findings.fix_check: Add pending_readiness to the Allowance type, render a truthful label (for example 'N awaiting readiness confirmation, already counted as used'), and assert it in the DOM test.

findings.title: No native evidence; probe and build not yet run on a passing tree
findings.problem: npm test exits 1, so the build, card adapter, retained probes, private_bridge_probe.mjs and the CUA scenarios (private-introduction, once-only-readiness, pending-hidden, original-recovery, frozen-revision, withdrawal-held-response) have no evidence. The report correctly claims nothing. The play-service Start boundary and the future 08-A limitation are disclosed in the docs and report, and the fixture keeps the raw play private with start/commit instrumentation, as required.
findings.fix_check: After attempt 3: all checks pass, private_bridge_probe passes, and CUA evidence is bound to the candidate blobs.

findings.title: Coverage: retained versus fresh reading for feature-r1
findings.problem: Retained from my own complete reads in setup r1–r4 of this session (unchanged since): the authority files, engineering v1.2 (four files), product/decisions, cards 05-B/08-A/08-B/00-B/00-C with contracts and screen map, the four slice records and 07-A/B status, and the app originals (review-service/journal, queue/continuation journals, generation/draft-fixture, request-queue/production-submission, entitlements, family-space, adult-access/http, play-service/catalog, migrations 001–015 and the loader, the FamilyHome/client tests), plus the Root probe, controller and runner. Read fresh this round, through EOF: the full diff of all 12 deliverables (the 8 new files are complete within it, and the hunks of the 4 edited files); review-service.mjs 60–359 (history, fenced, livePending, finish, currentPin, validatedGeneration); LoopFamilyHome.tsx 92–121 and its type and allowance lines; loop-generation-service.test.mjs 28–59 (fixture access policy and inbox); request-queue command shapes; migration 012 queue_namespace_guard; the family-space-client validation line; and the probe's fixture member usage, which is compatible. Limits: I ran nothing; test results are the controller's. Confirmed by code: Root's three suspicions and the two harness causes. Not exercised by me: the deferred-trigger performance, or whether the journal wrapper's wiping is safe against caching inside the inner review journal.
